guideTitle: 6 Best Gibson Dinnerware Sets for Home Tables (2026)
metaDescription: Six Gibson Home and Gibson Elite dinnerware sets compared by porcelain versus stoneware, piece count, mugs and care, from Ogalla to Oslo and Rockaway.
introParagraphs: Gibson sells dinnerware under two lines, Gibson Home and Gibson Elite, and the sets span white porcelain, matte stoneware and reactive glaze stoneware. This guide compares six: the Gibson Home Oslo 16-piece porcelain set, the Gibson Home Ogalla 30-piece service for six, the Gibson Home Rockaway 12-piece matte stoneware set, the Gibson Elite Soho Lounge 16-piece teal set, the Gibson Elite Matisse 16-piece blue reactive glaze set, and the Gibson Home Amelia Court square white set.

The spread shows up in piece count and mugs. The Ogalla offers 30 pieces for six, three sets list 16 pieces for four, and the Rockaway stops at 12 pieces. The Soho Lounge and Amelia Court include mugs, while the Ogalla also lists mugs among its pieces.
We evaluated each set based on product specs and buyer feedback, with attention to weight, bowl sizes, care guidance and style. We make no claim of lab testing.

products.name: Gibson Home Oslo 16-Piece Porcelain Set
products.description:
The Gibson Home Oslo is a porcelain service for four with 10.5 inch dinner plates, 7.75 inch dessert plates, 7.75 inch dinner bowls and 5.5 inch cereal bowls. Each piece has a hand painted navy blue rim for a French bistro look. The listing says the porcelain is chip and scratch resistant and microwave and dishwasher safe.

Having two bowl sizes makes the set flexible for soup and cereal. The tradeoff is that the painted rim may wear with heavy washing, and the set serves only four.

Porcelain is lighter than the stoneware sets here. Compared with the Rockaway, the Oslo offers more pieces and more bowl choices. It is the best all round pick.
products.bestFor: Everyday users who want light porcelain with two bowl sizes and clear care rules
pros: Navy rim adds a bistro look
cons: Painted rim may wear over time

products.name: Gibson Home Ogalla 30-Piece Porcelain Set for 6
products.description:
The Gibson Home Ogalla is a classic white coupe shaped service for six with 30 pieces. It includes six each of 10.25 inch dinner plates, 7.25 inch dessert plates, 6 inch bowls, 4.5 inch salad bowls and mugs. The listing describes AB-grade porcelain that is durable, lightweight and BPA free.

Five pieces per person make this the fullest set in the guide. The tradeoff is storage, since thirty pieces need a dedicated shelf, and the dinner plate is slightly smaller than the Oslo.

The white coupe shape stacks well. Compared with the Soho Lounge, the Ogalla serves two more people. Choose it for hosting.
products.bestFor: Households of six that want a complete white porcelain service with mugs
pros: Five pieces per person for six
Includes mugs and two bowl sizes
cons: Thirty pieces need lots of storage
Dinner plate is smaller than the Oslo
Care rules not stated in the listing

products.name: Gibson Home Rockaway 12-Piece Matte Stoneware Set
products.description:
The Gibson Home Rockaway is a white matte stoneware set with four each of 10.5 inch dinner plates, 8 inch dessert plates and 6 inch bowls that hold 26.5 ounces. The smooth, flat finish is dipped in solid color. The listing says it is microwave and dishwasher safe.

The bowl capacity is generous for a 6 inch size. The tradeoff is that stoneware is heavy and matte glazes can show marks.

Twelve pieces store compactly. Compared with the Oslo, the Rockaway has fewer pieces but a modern matte feel. Choose it for a small, modern table.
products.bestFor: Small households that want a modern matte white stoneware set

products.name: Gibson Elite Soho Lounge 16-Piece Teal Stoneware Set
products.description:
The Gibson Elite Soho Lounge in teal is a stoneware service for four with 11 inch dinner plates, 7.95 inch dessert plates, 5.5 inch bowls and 13.5 ounce mugs. The double reactive glaze gives each piece a vibrant, varied look. The listing says it is dishwasher and microwave safe.

The 11 inch plate is the largest in this guide. The tradeoff is that the 5.5 inch bowl is small and each piece varies in color.

Mugs are included, which helps coffee drinkers. Compared with the Oslo, the Soho Lounge has bigger plates but smaller bowls. Choose it for color and mugs.
products.bestFor: Coffee drinkers who want a colorful stoneware set with mugs
pros: 11 inch dinner plate is the largest here

products.name: Gibson Elite Matisse 16-Piece Blue Reactive Glaze Set
products.description:
The Gibson Elite Matisse is a blue reactive glaze stoneware service for four with 10.5 inch dinner plates, 8.5 inch dessert plates and two bowl sizes including a 5.25 inch bowl. The listing says reactive glaze lets multiple colors react for a dreamlike, vibrant quality. It is dishwasher and microwave safe.

The two bowl sizes add flexibility. Each piece differs slightly.

Sixteen pieces store compactly. Compared with the Soho Lounge, the Matisse has smaller plates but two bowls. Choose it for a bold blue.
products.bestFor: Buyers who want a bold blue reactive glaze set with two bowl sizes

products.name: Gibson Home Amelia Court Square White Porcelain Set
products.description:
The Gibson Home Amelia Court is a white square porcelain service for four with 9.5 inch dinner plates, 7 inch bowls and 12 ounce mugs. The listing describes AB-grade porcelain that is durable, lightweight and BPA free. It is chip and scratch resistant.

The square shape gives a clean look. The tradeoff is the smaller 9.5 inch plate and square corners that can catch in a rack.

Porcelain keeps the set light. Compared with the Rockaway, it includes mugs but smaller plates. Choose it for budget.
products.bestFor: Budget buyers who want a square white porcelain set with mugs
cons: 9.5 inch plate is the smallest here
Square corners can catch in a rack

buyingCriteria.explanation: The Oslo, Ogalla and Amelia Court are porcelain, while the Rockaway, Soho Lounge and Matisse are stoneware. Porcelain is lighter and stoneware is heavier. Choose porcelain for easy lifting. Stoneware suits a sturdy feel.
The Rockaway has 26.5 ounce bowls, the Oslo has 7.75 inch and 5.5 inch bowls, and the Soho Lounge has a 5.5 inch bowl. Two bowl sizes add flexibility. Small bowls frustrate soup lovers. Check sizes.
The Ogalla offers 30 pieces for six, and the Soho Lounge and Amelia Court include mugs. The Oslo has no mugs. Decide if you need mugs. Count settings.
Reactive glaze sets like the Matisse and Soho Lounge vary piece to piece. Matte sets like the Rockaway can show marks. White porcelain is the most uniform. Pick a look you will like.
The Oslo, Rockaway, Soho Lounge and Matisse state microwave and dishwasher safety. The Ogalla and Amelia Court do not. Check the label. Hand wash if unsure.
The Soho Lounge has an 11 inch plate, the Oslo has 10.5 inches, and the Amelia Court has a 9.5 inch square plate. Bigger plates hold more. Square plates need more rack room. Measure your cabinet.

howWeEvaluated.title: Material and weight
howWeEvaluated.description: The Oslo and Ogalla are porcelain, and the Rockaway is stoneware. We scored lighter sets higher.

howWeEvaluated.title: Bowl and plate sizing
howWeEvaluated.description: The Soho Lounge has the largest plate and the Rockaway has the largest bowl capacity. Sizes matter for real meals. Missing sizes lost points.

howWeEvaluated.title: Care guidance
howWeEvaluated.description: We checked microwave and dishwasher statements. Four sets had clear guidance. Two did not. Clear care earns credit.

howWeEvaluated.title: Completeness
howWeEvaluated.description: We counted pieces and mugs. The Ogalla has the most. The Rockaway has the fewest. Completeness matters for real use.

howWeEvaluated.title: Value
howWeEvaluated.description: The Amelia Court is lowest and the Matisse is highest. We favored sets that cover needs. Value also meant care clarity.

cards.label: Porcelain
cards.text: Lighter and crisp. Oslo, Ogalla and Amelia Court fall here. Choose it for easy lifting.

cards.label: Stoneware
cards.text: Heavier with color. Rockaway, Soho Lounge and Matisse fall here. Choose it for sturdy character.

howToChoose.note: Recommendation: pick Oslo for lighter handling and Soho Lounge for color and mugs.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Choose stated microwave and dishwasher safety, two bowl sizes and plates around 10.5 inches.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: Gibson Home Oslo is the best match with two bowl sizes and microwave and dishwasher safety.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You want a bold glaze, in which case the Matisse fits. Spend more on the Ogalla for six settings.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You want a simple set, where the Amelia Court or Rockaway fits at a lower tier.

faq.q: What is the difference between Gibson Home and Gibson Elite?
faq.a: Both are Gibson lines. Gibson Elite sets in this guide use reactive glaze stoneware. Gibson Home sets are mostly porcelain or matte stoneware.

faq.q: How do I choose between porcelain and stoneware?
faq.a: Porcelain is lighter and stoneware is heavier. The Oslo is porcelain and the Matisse is stoneware. Choose by weight.

faq.q: How much should I spend on Gibson dinnerware?
faq.a: In our data the Amelia Court is lowest and the Matisse is highest. More pieces and glazes cost more. Pick by need.
Four sets state microwave and dishwasher safety. Two do not. Check the label.
The Ogalla, Soho Lounge and Amelia Court include mugs. Others do not. Check each listing.

faq.q: Do reactive glaze sets match exactly?
faq.a: No. Reactive glaze varies piece to piece. That is part of the look.
